item.title: A2A Java SDK releases client and server support for agent communication
item.description:
A2A Java SDK releases client and server support for agent communication

A new Java library has been released to support the execution of agentic applications as Agent2Agent (A2A) servers. This multi-module Maven library provides both client and server capabilities, enabling A2A agent communication across JSON-RPC, gRPC, and REST transports.

🧩 How it works

The library facilitates agent-to-agent interaction by implementing the A2A Protocol. For gRPC support, the project copies the a2a.proto file from the A2A specification repository into the spec-grpc/ project. The java_package option is adjusted to target the org.a2aproject.sdk.grpc package. Developers can regenerate the gRPC classes by building the module with the command mvn clean install -Dskip.protobuf.generate=false.

⚙️ Key details

  • Language Requirement: Java 17 or later is required.
  • Transport Protocols: Supports JSON-RPC, gRPC, and REST.
  • Licensing: The project is licensed under the Apache 2.0 License.
  • Documentation: Full documentation is available at a2aproject.github.io/a2a-java.

🚀 Availability and Integrations

Developers can add the A2A Java SDK reference server for JSON-RPC to their Maven projects. The SDK includes examples for cross-language integration, such as a Java A2A server communicating with a Python client, and a Java A2A client communicating with a Python server.

Feature Details
OpenTelemetry Available as an optional add-on in the extras folder
JPA-backed task store Available as an optional add-on in the extras folder
Kafka-based replicated queue manager Available as an optional add-on in the extras folder
Vert.x and Android HTTP clients Available as optional add-ons in the extras folder

Integrations with Java runtimes are documented in the Server Integrations section of the reference materials.

#Java #AIagents #A2A #Maven #gRPC

Source: a2aproject/a2a-java

item.title: .NET SDK enables development of applications using the A2A v1.0 protocol
item.description:
.NET SDK enables development of applications using the A2A v1.0 protocol

A new .NET SDK has been released that allows developers to build and host applications following the Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol, providing a robust implementation of the specification v1.0.

🧩 How it works

The library supports multiple communication methods, allowing agents to interact through message-based or task-based patterns.

  • Agent Capability Discovery: Retrieves agent capabilities and metadata through agent cards.
  • Message-based Communication: Enables direct, stateless messaging with immediate responses.
  • Task-based Communication: Allows for the creation and management of persistent, long-running agent tasks.
  • Streaming Support: Facilitates real-time communication using Server-Sent Events.

⚙️ Key details

The SDK is built to integrate directly with web application stacks and supports multiple protocol bindings.

Component Description
A2AClient Primary client for making A2A requests to agents; supports streaming, non-streaming, and push notifications.
A2ACardResolver Resolves agent card information from A2A-compatible endpoints.
A2AServer Core server handling A2A JSON-RPC requests and coordinating task lifecycle.
IAgentHandler Interface for agents to implement, providing methods for message handling and task cancellation.
TaskUpdater API for emitting task lifecycle events such as start, complete, and fail.
MessageResponder API for sending stateless message replies without task lifecycle management.

All three protocol bindings—JSON-RPC, HTTP+JSON REST, and gRPC—share the same client contract and server pipeline. The gRPC binding is packaged as optional modules to prevent core consumers from being forced to depend on specific gRPC libraries.

🚀 Availability

The library targets .NET 8 and higher and includes built-in extensions for hosting A2A agents within web applications.

  • The v1.0 implementation is available as a NuGet package.
  • A backward-compatible package is available during the transition period.
  • A configuration option allows developers to explicitly request a completed task response when calling v1 servers from v0.3 clients, which helps avoid returning an incomplete initial task snapshot.

#dotnet #AIagents #A2A #softwaredevelopment #protocol

Source: a2aproject/a2a-dotnet

item.title: AWS Reference Architecture Connects Enterprise LangChain Orchestrator to SaaS Compliance Agent via A2A
item.description:
AWS Reference Architecture Connects Enterprise LangChain Orchestrator to SaaS Compliance Agent via A2A

A reference implementation on AWS demonstrates how the Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol lets an enterprise LangChain orchestrator work with a Strands Agents‑based compliance SaaS agent across separate AWS accounts.

🔍 Overview

  • Agents in multi‑agent systems that span organizational boundaries often need to collaborate in a composable, interoperable way, with agents that other organizations build and run.
  • The Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol addresses this constraint.
  • The A2A protocol is now a Linux Foundation project, and AWS is among the organizations that support it.

🧩 How it works

  • Three agents run in two AWS accounts, one for the enterprise and one for the SaaS provider.
  • Each account has its own Amazon Cognito user pool, so each side authenticates with its own identity provider.
  • During onboarding the enterprise and the SaaS provider exchange only public values, such as identity provider URLs, client IDs, scopes, and endpoint URLs.
  • The enterprise app gets an access token from the enterprise’s Amazon Cognito user pool.
  • The app sends a question over HTTPS to the user API in Amazon API Gateway, then polls for the answer.
  • Amazon API Gateway forwards the request privately, through a VPC link and an internal Network Load Balancer, to the Enterprise Orchestrator, a LangChain agent.
  • When its model decides that the question needs a compliance scan, the orchestrator gets its own token from the enterprise user pool, using a client secret stored in AWS Secrets Manager.
  • The orchestrator sends an A2A request to the compliance SaaS agent on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime, using the skill it read from the agent’s Agent Card at startup.
  • The compliance agent checks the enterprise context agent’s Agent Card at the callback URL registered at onboarding, then gets a token from the SaaS provider’s own pool.
  • The compliance agent calls back to the enterprise context agent for account metadata, finishes its scan, and returns the answer to the orchestrator and then to the app.
  • Both enterprise agents run on Amazon ECS with AWS Fargate in private subnets of an Amazon VPC, with no public IP addresses.
  • The SaaS agent reaches the context agent through an API Gateway partner API that accepts only the SaaS provider’s callback token.

⚙️ Key details

  • Deployed agent uses the official a2a-sdk (AgentCard, AgentExecutor, and spec-conformant JSON-RPC routes), pinned to a2a-sdk[http-server]==1.2.2.
  • At startup the orchestrator fetches the SaaS agent’s Agent Card from its well‑known URL and creates a LangChain tool for each skill described on the card.
Agent Runtime / Framework Model Role
Enterprise Orchestrator LangChain on Amazon ECS (Fargate) Anthropic Claude Sonnet 4.6 (Bedrock) Receives user queries, decides when to invoke compliance scan
Enterprise Context Agent LangChain on Amazon ECS (Fargate) Amazon Nova Lite (Bedrock) Provides internal account metadata, policy rules, data classification
Compliance SaaS Agent Strands Agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore – Performs compliance scan and returns results

🚀 Availability

  • The protocol uses existing authentication standards such as OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect (OIDC) for cross‑boundary security, and is designed to work across A2A‑compatible frameworks.
  • Independent software vendors (ISVs) can build composable, interoperable agents that work with the A2A‑compatible frameworks their customers already use.

💡 Why it matters

  • Neither side depends on the other’s framework or SDK, and the two sides share no secrets.
  • The architecture shows how organizations can keep agents isolated in private subnets while still enabling secure, standards‑based cross‑account collaboration.

#AWS #A2A #LangChain #Bedrock

Source: Build composable, interoperable multi-agent systems with A2A on AWS | Amazon Web Services

item.title: a2a-adapter Enables Easy A2A Protocol Integration for Local AI Agents
item.description:
a2a-adapter Enables Easy A2A Protocol Integration for Local AI Agents

The new a2a-adapter tool wraps existing agent CLIs, local agents, workflow engines, and Python agent frameworks behind the A2A (Agent-to-Agent) Protocol.

🔍 Overview

  • Provides automatic AgentCard generation, JSON‑RPC handling, task lifecycle management, and streaming via the official A2A SDK.
  • Your adapter only needs to invoke the underlying agent; a2a‑adapter takes care of the A2A plumbing.

🧩 How It Works

  1. Install a2a-adapter into your project’s virtual environment (Python 3.11+ required).
  2. Wrap your existing agent with the adapter and start the server.
  3. The adapter exposes the agent as an A2A server, e.g., http://localhost:9000, with an auto‑generated Agent Card at http://localhost:9000/.well-known/agent-card.json.
  4. The server can be mounted inside an existing ASGI app using to_a2a(adapter).

⚙️ Supported Agents

  • Claude Code
  • Codex
  • Pi
  • OpenClaw
  • n8n
  • LangGraph
  • LangChain
  • CrewAI
  • Ollama
  • Hermes Agent
  • Custom Python functions

🚀 Installation & Usage

  • Install the CLI as an isolated tool so the a2a-adapter command is on your PATH.
  • Upgrade later with uv tool upgrade a2a-adapter.
  • Avoid system‑wide pip install because macOS’s built‑in pip runs Python 3.9 (too old) and many Linux distributions block it (PEP 668).
  • Ensure the underlying agent works on its own; a2a-adapter does not install the agent.
    • Example: install Claude Code and run claude once to sign in.
  • If the agent executable is not on PATH, specify it with --executable /path/to/agent.
  • Start the server from the project directory where the agent should run.
  • Options placed before -- configure the A2A server; options placed after -- are passed to the underlying agent CLI.
  • Run a2a-adapter -help for a list of supported agents, or a2a-adapter <agent> -help for agent‑specific usage.

💡 Why It Matters

  • A single adaptor turns any compatible local agent into an A2A‑compliant service without modifying the agent code.
  • The same A2A server interface works for both classic local agents (Claude Code, Codex, Pi, OpenClaw) and modern Python‑based frameworks.
  • By providing a standard Agent Card at /.well-known/agent-card.json, the adapter enables discovery and integration in broader A2A ecosystems.

#A2A #AIAgents #Python #Tooling

Source: hybroai/a2a-adapter
